name: Draft and check AI replies to Google reviews with Gmail, OpenAI and Google Sheets

parameters.content:
## Draft AI replies to Google reviews — you stay in control

### How it works
Google emails you when your business gets a new review. This workflow watches Gmail for those alerts, has AI write a reply draft that is written to follow Google's reply-moderation rules, and emails the draft to you. You read it, tweak it, and paste it on Google. **Nothing is ever posted automatically** — the draft lands in your inbox and a row lands in your Google Sheets ledger. The ledger is also the guard: an alert that is already logged is never processed twice.

### Setup
1. Connect **Gmail** and **Google Sheets** (one-click Google sign-in).
2. Add your **OpenAI API key** to the model node.
3. Create a Google Sheet with a tab named exactly `reviews` and headers: `processed_at, gmail_message_id, rating, reviewer, review_excerpt, reply_draft, status`.
4. Fill in **⚙️ Your settings**: business name, your email, tone, contact channel, and paste the sheet URL into **sheetUrl**. That is the only place you name the sheet — never pick one inside a Sheets node.
5. Open every node showing a ⚠️ once (both Gmail nodes, both Sheets nodes, the OpenAI model) so your credential is attached; leave URL and tab fields as they are. n8n will not activate a workflow with an unattached credential.
6. To test **before activating**, click *Execute workflow*: the trigger fetches your most recent review alert and the whole flow runs once. Run it again to see the ledger guard skip it. Once activated, only alerts arriving **after** activation are picked up. Forwarding an alert to yourself does **not** work (it comes from your own address).

### Customization tips
Adjust tone and sign-off in ⚙️ Your settings; swap the model node for Gemini or Claude.

## 1. Catch + guard
Gmail trigger fires on Google's "new review" notification emails. Before anything is drafted, the ledger is read once and compared in code — a review that is already in the ledger is never processed twice (no duplicate drafts in your inbox), and several alerts arriving together are each handled on their own.

## 2. Think
One AI call extracts the rating, reviewer name and review text from the alert email, then drafts a reply that follows Google's moderation rules: references a concrete detail, no links, no promotions, apologetic-but-not-liable for 1–2★. Uses your business name, tone and contact channel from ⚙️ Your settings.

## 3. Deliver + log
The draft is emailed to you with a one-click link to your Google reviews page, then one row is built and appended to your Google Sheets ledger — so you can see every review, every draft, and what you did with it.

parameters.text:
=You are drafting a public reply to a Google review on behalf of {{ $('⚙️ Your settings').first().json.businessName }}.

Below is the full text of a Google Business Profile "new review" notification email. First extract: the star rating (1-5), the reviewer's first name, and the review text. Then write reply_draft following ALL rules.

Rules for the reply:
- Tone: {{ $('⚙️ Your settings').first().json.brandTone }}. Maximum 110 words.
- Address the reviewer by first name only (privacy: never use a full name).
- Reference one concrete detail from their review. Never write a reply that could fit any review — generic AI boilerplate gets rejected by Google's reply moderation.
- Never include: links, promotions, discounts, upsells, keyword stuffing, or requests to change the rating (these also get rejected).
- 4-5 stars: thank them warmly and specifically.
- 3 stars: thank them, acknowledge the specific gap they mention, state one concrete improvement.
- 1-2 stars: apologize sincerely without admitting legal fault, address their specific issue, invite them to continue the conversation offline: {{ $('⚙️ Your settings').first().json.contactChannel }}.
- End with: {{ $('⚙️ Your settings').first().json.signOff }}
- Plain text only: no HTML, no markdown, no emoji.

NOTIFICATION EMAIL:
{{ $json.text }}
